title: Share validated streamed Claude runtime source discovery
description: Objective: add one internal runner primitive that discovers caller-named Claude runtime source candidates through the same Windows path/containment/reparse/canonicalization authority used by runtime pinning, then streams their digests without first reading an unvalidated path. Refactor the existing quote-resolution path to share that primitive, preserving its behavior. This is the prerequisite for task-32eddfd3c9644558b7218778e1f07e92; it does not observe a version, spawn a process, define the installed-runtime closure, publish a package-root API, or grant launch authority. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-runtime-pin-closure.ts/.js, claude-runtime-source.ts/.js, and claude-runtime-source.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: An internal bounded discovery function accepts at most MAX_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_ENTRIES caller-named kind/path candidates and one canonical installed root, validates path shape, containment, every segment, entry kind, realpath identity, and duplicates before streaming any bytes, then returns sorted immutable SourceEntry records with production SHA-256 digests.

The existing resolveSources quote path delegates to the same source-inspection authority and preserves exact success ordering plus every existing stable CLAUDE_RUNTIME_* refusal code and RUNTIME layer; no parallel path/reparse/digest policy remains.

Malformed, empty, overflow, duplicate, missing, non-file, reparse/junction, escape, unreadable, and drift/race cases fail closed with exact stable code and layer; tests assert no source read before validation and positive generated case counts.
Mutation drills against the production surface prove the tests fail if segment validation, canonical containment, streamed digesting, or the shared resolveSources delegation is bypassed.
Both production TypeScript modules remain below 250 physical lines, each JavaScript bridge remains one line, and the runner plus repository typecheck gates execute with a nonzero test count.
taskRails: TDD every change; refusal tests assert exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and every generated sweep asserts a positive case count.
Keep the primitive internal to @moe/runner: no bare-root export, caller filesystem/process/clock port, closure-classification policy, launch, or authority.

Use the existing ClaudeRuntimeFsPort, streamDigest, Windows path rules, and refusal vocabulary; refactor shared authority instead of copying it. Preserve foreign work and commit only the five explicit owned paths.

- Happy path: 3 scrambled candidates return sorted-by-relativePath frozen entries with LITERAL digests b80935d4…(70000-byte executable), 6ad39cb8…(launcher), 73be916e…(package); array and every entry Object.isFrozen.
- Bounded streaming: exactly 3 readChunks calls, max chunk <= RUNTIME_PIN_CHUNK_BYTES (65536), >=4 chunks total and an exact total byte sum — a materialising read cannot satisfy both.
- 12-row shape matrix, all pinned to CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_INVALID@RUNTIME with truthClass UNKNOWN and ZERO readChunks: non-array/string/null, empty, MAX_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_ENTRIES+1 overflow, non-record element, extra key, accessor-defined path, get-trapping Proxy, unknown kind, non-string path, missing kind.

The traversal row is built by STRING CONCATENATION, not win32.join, because join normalises the `..` away and the row would silently stop testing traversal (this exact defect is recorded in mem:gotcha-windows-path-identity-in-the-runner-pin).
- Fault/race cases: entryKind throwing => PATH_MISSING with 0 reads; readChunks throwing mid-stream => SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH; leaf replaced by a junction after the read, leaf deleted after the read, and realpath answering a different file on the post-read call => all three CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_SOURCE_DRIFT.
- PARITY: resolveSources and discoverSources on equivalent fixtures must produce an IDENTICAL ordered fs trace (entryKind/realpath/readChunks) and identical entries, plus explicit ordinal assertions that the read happens AFTER the first realpath and BEFORE the last realpath — i.e. the read is fenced on both sides. This is what makes "no parallel path/digest policy remains" testable rather than asserted by inspection.

Fixtures use real temporary files behind the production Node adapter via createEmulatedWin32RuntimeFs; the only additions are counting and fault wrappers, no reimplementation of any production rule.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the minimum shared inspection engine in `claude-runtime-source.ts` with a one-line `.js` bridge. Move (do not clone) Windows fold/path-shape/containment, segment walking, SourceEntry/sorting, and streamed source inspection out of the closure module. Strictly snapshot a plain bounded candidate array (1..MAX_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_ENTRIES) of exact `{kind,path}` records before I/O; reject malformed shapes with `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_INVALID`, then for each case-folded unique path validate local-drive form, containment, every directory/leaf kind, and canonical realpath identity before `streamDigest`. Catch pre-read fs failures as `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING`, catch read failures as `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, re-run the segment/canonical identity checks after the stream and map any change/failure to `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_SOURCE_DRIFT`; compare an optional expected digest only after the stable inspection. Return sorted copies with every entry and the array frozen. The engine returns an internal code/message failure for its caller to wrap—no runtime import from closure, public root export, filesystem implementation, directory enumeration, process/clock port, logging, or authority.
implementationPlan.note:
Shared inspection engine implemented in claude-runtime-source.ts (250 physical lines, exactly at the cap) with a one-line `.js` bridge matching the directory convention (`export * from "./claude-runtime-source.ts";`).

MOVED, NOT CLONED: fold, LOCAL_ABSOLUTE + pathShapeRejection, isInside, segmentRejection, byRelativePath, SourceEntry and the streamed inspection now live here only. Step 4 deletes them from closure and re-exports, so no parallel path/reparse/digest policy survives.

PUBLIC ENGINE SURFACE: RuntimeSourceCandidate, InspectedCandidate, SourceEntry, SourceInspectionFailure, fold, pathShapeRejection, isInside, snapshotSourceCandidates, inspectSources. No bare-root export, no fs implementation, no directory enumeration, no process/clock port, no logging, no authority.

ESM CYCLE AVOIDED DELIBERATELY: `verbatimModuleSyntax: true` is set in tsconfig.base.json, which means the inline `import { type X }` form KEEPS the import statement at runtime — that would have made source<->closure a genuine ESM cycle. The error-code type is therefore imported with the statement form `import type { ClaudeRuntimePinErrorCode }`, which is always fully erased. The engine returns a bare `{code, message}` SourceInspectionFailure and never imports `refuse` at runtime, so the closure module remains the sole owner of the refusal shape and vocabulary.

ORDER, which is the actual security property: shape -> case-folded duplicate -> containment -> segment walk -> canonical realpath identity -> streamDigest -> RE-PROVE segment+realpath -> compare expected digest. Identical to today's resolveOne up to the stream, with two additions the plan required and step 1 flagged as currently-missing: the post-read re-proof and the fs-failure catches.

FAILURE MAPPING: pre-read fs throw => CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING (an unreadable entry is indistinguishable from an absent one; neither can be hashed). Read throw => CLAUDE_RUNTIME_SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH, so a partial read can never escape as a partial digest. Any post-read identity change OR throw => CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_SOURCE_DRIFT. Expected-digest comparison happens LAST, only after the inspection is stable — comparing earlier would let a drifting path be reported as a mere digest mismatch.

HOSTILE-INPUT SNAPSHOT: snapshotSourceCandidates requires a real Array of 1..MAX_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_ENTRIES(64) elements and copies each as an exact 2-key {kind,path} record. Values are read from `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors`, never through `get`, so an accessor cannot hand validation one path and the stream another; a descriptor that is not a data descriptor is refused. `types.isProxy` refuses a proxy outright, following the existing precedent in this same directory (claude-launcher-port-results.ts:50,83) and wrapped in try/catch the same way. kind must be a member of RUNTIME_CLOSURE_KINDS.

IMMUTABILITY: every entry is Object.freeze'd at construction and the returned array is frozen after sorting. Verified no existing consumer mutates the result (grep for push/sort/splice/pop/shift/index-assign over the sources value in claude-runtime-pin.ts and claude-runtime-pin-copy.ts found nothing), so freezing the shared return is safe for the quote path too.

Not yet wired: closure still holds its own copies, so the focused suite is still RED by design. Step 4 performs the delegation.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review found a real defect, I fixed it, and per this step's own instruction I then REPEATED the entire step against the changed code. Everything below is from the second, post-fix pass.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED — index correspondence against a hostile array-like. `resolveSources` snapshotted `{kind,path}` from `closure.map(...)` but then reached BACK into the caller's array with `closure[index]?.sha256` to attach the expected digest. A hostile array-like (Proxy) can answer position `index` with a different entry on the second read, pairing one entry's VALIDATED path with another entry's declared digest — the exact "snapshot before iteration" class the task risks call out. Fixed by copying kind/path/sha256 out in ONE pass into a plain local `declared` array and indexing only that. Low exploitability today (the only caller passes readQuote's canonically-validated closure) but the primitive is now directly callable, and fail-closed is the epic's posture.

New test pins it: a Proxy array that answers position 0 with the honest entry first and a digest-swapped entry afterwards must still resolve to the honest digest. Focused suite grew 37 -> 38.

FIVE MUTATION DRILLS, all with an out-of-repository backup, recorded SHA-256, EXIT restore trap, and an exactly-one-replacement guard that aborts if the anchor is not unique. Every drill executed a NONZERO test count and failed on its exact assertion:
(a) segment validation bypassed -> "a directory in a file position" red: expected CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_NOT_FILE, got CLAUDE_RUNTIME_SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH (1 failed | 37 skipped).
(b) post-read identity re-proof bypassed -> all THREE drift cases red, each receiving a successful entry where a refusal was required (3 failed | 35 skipped).
(c) real streamDigest replaced by a constant -> "pinned digests" red on the literal-digest array (1 failed | 37 skipped).
(d) resolveSources expected-digest delegation bypassed -> "quoted digest that does not match" red (1 failed | 37 skipped).
(e) single-pass capture reverted to re-indexing the caller array -> the new pairing test red with CLAUDE_RUNTIME_SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH (1 failed | 37 skipped). This one proves the fix itself is load-bearing rather than decorative.

Measured cause: 54 links under node_modules were WSL-style symlinks that Windows Node cannot traverse (`Get-Item` reports `Attributes: Directory, ReparsePoint` with EMPTY LinkType/Target; `fs.statSync` -> EACCES), and several pointed at long-form virtual-store dirs that do not exist on Windows (e.g. `@vitest+mocker@4.1.10_vite@8.2.1_@types+node@24.13.3_yaml@2.9.0_` vs the hashed `@vitest+mocker@4.1.10_vite@_d214c711e4d7a93d53ea3181d095a7c8`). Because this edited a test, I re-ran mutation drill (b) from step 5 against the changed file: replacing `const drift = await identityRejection(fs, realRoot, candidate.path);` with `const drift = null;` (anchor count asserted == 1) reddened 4 named tests — all three drift cases INCLUDING the changed junction case, plus the resolveSources/discoverSources parity case — `Tests 4 failed | 34 passed (38)`.
